story.title: From Sea to Shore in Duqm: OMR 5.4 Million Coastal Fishing Project Pairs Tuna and Cuttlefish Processing With Artisan Safety at Sea
story.seo_title: Duqm OMR 5.4M Coastal Fishing & Artisan Safety Project
story.meta_description: Oman signs an OMR 5.43 million integrated tuna and cuttlefish processing agreement in Duqm alongside three partnerships for artisanal fishermen safety.

detail.extracted_title: From Sea to Shore in Duqm: OMR 5.4 Million Coastal Fishing Project Pairs Tuna and Cuttlefish Processing With Artisan Safety at Sea
detail.excerpt: A new investment agreement in the Fisheries Industrial Zone at Duqm builds dedicated tuna and cuttlefish processing lines alongside three five-year partnerships equipping Oman's traditional fishermen with maritime safety gear, training, and economic support.
detail.article_html:
Along the Arabian Sea coast of Al Wusta Governorate, the work of fishing begins long before dawn. Small fiberglass skiffs and coastal vessels push out from sandy beaches and landing sites into deep waters rich in yellowfin tuna and cuttlefish. For decades, much of what Omani artisanal fishermen hauled aboard was sold raw at the water's edge, leaving the value of processing, packaging, and export to facilities far from the landing shore.

Yesterday, the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources took two connected steps to strengthen both ends of that coastal chain: signing an OMR 5.43 million investment agreement to build an integrated coastal fishing and seafood processing plant in Duqm, alongside three cooperation agreements dedicated to the safety, training, and economic livelihoods of Oman's artisanal fishermen.

Processing Tuna and Cuttlefish Where They Land

Signed by His Excellency Eng. Yaqoob bin Khalfan Al Busaidi, Undersecretary of the Ministry for Fisheries, and Mohammed bin Sabr Al Wahaibi, Chairman of the Board of Al Sawari International Company, the investment agreement establishes an integrated coastal fishing project inside the Fisheries Industrial Zone in Duqm at an investment value of approximately OMR 5,430,000.

The project includes a modern facility for preparing and packaging tuna and cuttlefish, paired with a dedicated production line for value-added cuttlefish products. By processing the catch directly within Duqm's fisheries hub, the plant keeps greater economic value inside the local supply chain, creates downstream industrial jobs, and supports Oman's food security and marine export goals.

Five Years of Maritime Safety and the "Zad Al Bahhar" Initiative

Recognizing that a resilient fisheries sector depends first on the people who go to sea, the Ministry signed three companion cooperation agreements yesterday focused on artisanal fishermen across Oman's coastal governorates. Through a five-year partnership with Asyad Shipping signed by CEO Dr. Ibrahim bin Bakhit Al Nadhairi, artisanal fishermen will receive integrated packages of essential marine safety equipment alongside coastal awareness and emergency response training.

In parallel, the Ministry partnered with Al Jisr Foundation, represented by Director General Dina bint Fawzi Al Khalili, to launch the Zad Al Bahhar ("Fisherman's Provision") initiative, upgrading the professional, productive, and administrative skills of traditional fishermen to sustain and diversify their household income. A third agreement with Development Bank, signed by CEO Hussain bin Ali bin Ibrahim Al Lawati, supports capacity building and the modernization of fishing operations across Oman's coast.

Together, the Duqm processing plant and the three artisan support programs link industrial scale with coastal community care—ensuring that when Omani fishermen return to shore with their catch, they do so with safer boats, stronger skills, and a local industry ready to carry their harvest to the world.

detail.instagram_caption:
In the Fisheries Industrial Zone at Duqm, a new OMR 5.43 million investment agreement is connecting the daily harvest of Oman's coastal waters with local processing and artisan safety at sea. Signed yesterday by the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources with Al Sawari International Company, the project establishes an integrated coastal fishing complex featuring a modern plant for preparing and packaging tuna and cuttlefish alongside a dedicated value-added cuttlefish production line.

Alongside the industrial facility in Duqm, the Ministry signed three companion cooperation agreements focused on the people who sustain Oman's maritime economy: artisanal fishermen. Through a five-year partnership with Asyad Shipping, traditional fishing crews across coastal governorates will receive integrated packages of marine safety equipment paired with emergency response and sea safety training.

Two additional agreements—launching the "Zad Al Bahhar" empowerment initiative with Al Jisr Foundation and a capacity-building program with Development Bank—will equip Omani fishermen with upgraded technical, administrative, and operational tools to strengthen their household livelihoods and sustain coastal communities for the long term.
